growing_conditions.location: Buon Ma Thuot, Dak Lak, Vietnam (12.68N, 108.04E)

crop.stage_note: harvest and sun-drying: excess rain delays picking and causes mold in drying yards — wetness is the risk, not drought
crop.method: 30-day rainfall anomaly weighted by the Dak Lak robusta phenology calendar (drought-sensitive flowering/fruit-set, wetness-sensitive harvest)

forecast.note: forward-looking model output; verified against realized rainfall in the public track record as windows close

brief: Coffee futures closed at 306¢/lb — up 0.1% on the week and up 11.1% on the month. The regime model reads the market as crisis and has for 29 sessions. Growing conditions look unremarkable: Central Highlands rainfall is near its seasonal norm (+0.5σ). The crop is in its maturation & harvest window, and stage-weighted stress is low. A strengthening Brazilian real (-3.9% in a month) squeezes producer margins — supportive for prices. Looking ahead: the 14-day forecast calls for 22 mm of rain in the robusta belt against a 82 mm seasonal norm (-1.0σ) — projected crop stress: low (Open-Meteo forecast model, issued 2026-10-23; skill scored publicly as windows close).
